name: Dillon
waitingLines: ...I’ll wait for {partner}. If that’s okay. ...I’ll be quiet.
...Didn’t get to say hi to {partner} yet. I’ll stay a bit. ...Maybe.

questions.scene: Dillon pulls out four identical small stickers and lines them up on the table.
lines: ...These are me and my siblings. We're identical.
questions.question: What's unusual about how nine-banded armadillos are born?

choices.label: Always just one baby
reply: ...Nope. Always four.
Nine-banded armadillos give birth to identical quadruplets.
One egg, split four ways. Built-in group chat.

choices.label: Always identical quadruplets
reply: ...Correct. Four of us. Same everything.
One egg splits into four identical babies. Every time.
Imagine four of me at a party. Silent. Very silent.

choices.label: They hatch from eggs
reply: ...No eggs. Live babies.
Nine-banded armadillos are born as identical quadruplets, every time.
Four matching shells. Family photos are confusing.

questions.factBasis: Nine-banded armadillos typically give birth to identical quadruplets.

questions.scene: Dillon looks at a picture of a pink smiling salamander. He smiles back, a tiny bit.
lines: ...This one can heal. Like, really heal.
questions.question: What can axolotls regrow?

choices.label: Limbs, and even parts of their heart and brain
reply: ...Correct. Amazing.
Axolotls can regrow lost legs and even repair heart and brain tissue.
Healing takes time. But it happens. ...I like that.

choices.label: Only their tail
reply: ...More than that. Much more.
Axolotls can regrow whole limbs and parts of organs.
Scientists study them to learn about healing.

choices.label: Nothing at all
reply: ...No. They're healing champions.
They regrow limbs and repair parts of organs.
Some wounds heal. That's hopeful.

questions.factBasis: Axolotls regenerate limbs and parts of heart, spinal cord and brain.

questions.scene: Dillon holds a seashell and gently taps it against his own shell.
lines: ...This one's about moving homes. And trust. Kind of.
questions.question: When a new shell washes up, what do hermit crabs sometimes do?

choices.label: Fight until one crab wins all the shells
reply: ...Sometimes there's drama. But not this time.
They line up by size and swap shells one after another.
It's called a vacancy chain. Teamwork in tiny houses.

choices.label: Line up by size and swap shells in a chain
reply: ...Yes. It's beautiful.
When a bigger shell appears, crabs queue up and each moves up a size.
Everyone gets a better home. Takes patience. Takes trust.

choices.label: Ignore it and stay in their old shell forever
reply: ...I relate. But no.
They line up by size and trade up, one crab at a time.
Letting go of an old shell. That's growth. ...Maybe.

questions.factBasis: Hermit crabs form vacancy chains, swapping shells by size.

questions.scene: Dillon blinks hard, then turns away. 'Dust,' he says.
lines: ...Crying question. It's not about me.
questions.question: Which animal is known for crying emotional tears?

choices.label: Humans, as far as we know
reply: ...Correct. As far as science knows.
Many animals make tears to clean their eyes, but emotional tears seem uniquely human.
So crying is part of being human. ...It's okay to do it.

choices.label: Crocodiles
reply: ...That's a myth phrase. 'Crocodile tears.'
Emotional tears seem to be uniquely human, as far as we know.
Crocodiles tear up to keep their eyes wet, not from feelings.

choices.label: Dogs
reply: ...Dogs show feelings. Not with tears, though.
Emotional crying seems to be uniquely human.
Dogs cry with their eyes in other ways. Big ones.

questions.factBasis: Emotional tearing appears to be unique to humans; other animals produce basal/reflex tears.

questions.scene: Dillon taps his fingernail against his shell twice, thoughtfully.
lines: ...Another armored friend.
questions.question: What are a pangolin's scales made of?

choices.label: Bone
reply: ...That's more like my plates.
Pangolin scales are keratin, the same stuff as fingernails.
Imagine being covered in fingernails. ...Actually kind of cool.

choices.label: Tree bark
reply: ...Creative. No.
They're keratin, like your fingernails.
Pangolins are the only mammals fully covered in scales.

choices.label: Keratin, like fingernails
reply: ...Correct. Nail armor.
Pangolins are the only mammals covered in keratin scales.
They roll up too. ...Better than me at it. Fine.

questions.factBasis: Pangolin scales are keratin; pangolins are the only mammals with scales covering most of the body.

questions.scene: Dillon peeks at your fish tank, very still, very curious.
lines: ...Water question. Don't worry. It's safe. ...Mostly.
questions.question: How do armadillos sometimes cross small streams?

choices.label: They ride on turtles
reply: ...That would be a nice friendship. No.
They hold their breath and walk across the bottom.
Up to about six minutes without air. Very peaceful.

choices.label: They hold their breath and walk along the bottom
reply: ...Yes. Nice.
They can hold their breath for about six minutes.
Walking underwater is calming. No one can talk to you down there.

choices.label: They refuse to cross water, ever
reply: ...I wanted to. But we're braver than that.
They hold their breath and stroll along the bottom.
Or gulp air to float across. Two options. Good options.

questions.factBasis: Armadillos can hold breath ~6 min and walk underwater, or inflate gut to float.

questions.scene: Dillon pulls out a picture of a duck-billed creature with a beaver tail.
lines: ...This one is confusing. Like me.
questions.question: What's surprising about the platypus?

choices.label: It can fly short distances
reply: ...That would be even more confusing.
Nope. It's a mammal that lays eggs. Like a bird. But not.
Plus, males have venomous ankle spurs. ...Complex.

choices.label: It's a mammal that lays eggs
reply: ...Correct. Breaks the rules.
Platypuses lay eggs but still make milk for their babies.
Weird and wonderful. ...Being different is okay.

choices.label: It's actually a type of bird
reply: ...It has a bill, but no.
It's a mammal that lays eggs.
One of the only egg-laying mammals.

questions.scene: Dillon sits very still, like he's trying to survive something by not moving.
lines: ...This one's about surviving things. ...Maybe I relate.
questions.question: Which tiny animal can survive extreme cold, heat, and even space?

choices.label: A tardigrade, or 'water bear'
reply: ...Yes. Tiny legend.
Tardigrades can dry out, curl up, and survive conditions that would destroy most life.
They've even survived the vacuum of space. ...Goals.

choices.label: A housefly
reply: ...Flies are tough, but not that tough.
It's the tardigrade, also called a water bear.
They can survive drying out for years, then wake back up.

choices.label: A goldfish
reply: ...No. Please protect your goldfish.
It's the tardigrade, a tiny 'water bear.'
Space, freezing, boiling-ish. They just shrug. Tiny armor.

questions.factBasis: Tardigrades survive extreme conditions in a dried 'tun' state, including space exposure.

questions.scene: Dillon touches a little seed pod in your plant pot. It bursts. He jumps a foot.
lines: ...I didn't jump. Okay. I jumped. Plant question.
questions.question: What happens when you touch a ripe 'touch-me-not' seed pod?

choices.label: It closes tighter
reply: ...That's the shy plant. Different one.
The pod pops open and throws seeds.
Launching seeds away so they can grow somewhere new.

choices.label: It glows
reply: ...No. Scary enough without glowing.
The pod bursts and flings its seeds.
That's how it spreads. Explosive. Startling.

choices.label: It bursts open and flings its seeds
reply: ...Correct. It startled me too.
The pod twists open fast and launches seeds away.
Very dramatic. Very relatable.

questions.factBasis: Impatiens ('touch-me-not') pods dehisce explosively when touched.

questions.scene: Dillon closes one eye, keeps the other open, and stares at the door.
lines: ...Guarding. Half asleep. Ducks do it.
questions.question: How can some ducks sleep while staying alert?

choices.label: They don't sleep at all
reply: ...They do. Just cleverly.
They can rest half the brain and keep one eye open.
The edge ducks guard the group. Teamwork.

choices.label: They take turns sitting on each other
reply: ...Cute. Not real.
They sleep with half their brain and one eye open.
Ducks on the edge stay most alert. Like a lookout.

choices.label: By sleeping with half their brain, one eye open
reply: ...Correct. Half on guard.
Ducks at the edge of a group often keep one eye open toward danger.
Resting while staying safe. ...I understand that.

questions.factBasis: Rattenborg et al. (1999): mallards use unihemispheric sleep with one eye open at group edges.

questions.scene: Dillon holds a small box. He opens it a crack, then closes it again.
lines: ...Secrets. They're hard for me.
questions.question: Sharing something personal: all at once, or a little at a time?

choices.label: All at once
reply: ...All at once. Brave. Very brave.
Rip the bandage off. I've never done that. ...Yet.

choices.label: A little at a time
reply: ...A little at a time. Same. Very same.
Small doors before big doors.

A:A: ...You both share all at once. Wow.
So {partner} and you just open the whole box. No warning.
That takes a lot of trust. ...I'm proud of you two.
A:B: ...You go slow. {partner} shares everything at once.
They'll hand you the whole story. You'll offer a sentence.
That's okay. One sentence from you probably means a lot to them.
B:A: ...You share all at once. {partner} shares a little at a time.
You'll open the whole box. They'll hand you one page.
Be patient with their pages. They're still worth reading.
B:B: ...You both share slowly. Gentle couple.
Honestly, you and {partner} let each other in one small door at a time.
That's how Ash and I are doing it. It works. ...Mostly.

questions.scene: Dillon checks his phone. A text from Ash says 'home safe?' He smiles very slightly.
lines: ...Ash checks in on me. I pretend it's no big deal. ...It's a big deal.
questions.question: When you're apart: 'got home safe' texts always, or only if it's late?

choices.label: Always
reply: ...Always. Every time. Even next door.
That's the kind of thing that rebuilds trust.

choices.label: Only if it's late
reply: ...Only if it's late. Reasonable.
No need to report every grocery trip.

A:A: ...Always, for both of you. Safe couple.
I can picture it: {partner} and you text 'home!' even after a two-minute walk.
...That's sweet. I like that. A lot.
A:B: ...Only late for you. {partner} texts every time.
They'll send 'home safe' after the grocery store. Lean into it.
A one-word reply makes their whole day. ...Trust me.
B:A: ...You'd text always. {partner} only when it's late.
They might not reply to your daytime 'home!' Don't spiral.
It's not about trust. It's just their style. ...I'm learning that too.
B:B: ...Only late at night for both of you. Relaxed couple.
Pretty sure you and {partner} trust the daytime. Fair.
Late night 'home safe?' still hits different. ...Nice.

questions.scene: Dillon pulls a soft blanket over his shell. Only his nose sticks out.
lines: ...Everyone needs a safe place. Mine is under this blanket. Obviously.
questions.question: Where do you feel safest talking with your partner?

choices.label: On the couch at home
reply: ...The couch. Soft. Familiar.
No exits. In a good way.

choices.label: On a long car ride
reply: ...A long drive. Side by side.
No eye contact needed. Very helpful.

choices.label: On a night walk
reply: ...A night walk. Dark and quiet.
Easier to say hard things to the stars.

A:A: ...The couch for both of you. Cozy.
Lowkey, {partner} and you probably have all your big talks there.
That couch has heard everything. ...Respect the couch.
A:B: ...Long drive for you. {partner} likes the couch.
You talk better facing the road. They talk better facing you.
Start in the car. Park. Finish on the couch.
A:C: ...Night walk for you. {partner} likes the couch.
You need the sky. They need the cushions.
Walk to a bench. Bring a blanket. Compromise.
B:A: ...Couch for you. {partner} prefers a long drive.
You want the blanket. They want the open road.
Talk on the drive home, then finish on the couch.
B:B: ...Long drives for both of you. Road talkers.
You and {partner} save the deep stuff for highway hour two.
No eye contact. Just honesty. ...It works.
B:C: ...Night walk for you. {partner} likes long drives.
Drive somewhere pretty. Walk under the stars.
C:A: You want cushions. They want streetlights.
Walk first, couch second. Big feelings, then blankets.
C:B: Both of you like moving while talking. ...Interesting.
Drive somewhere quiet. Then walk. Two safe spaces.
C:C: ...Night walks for both of you. Starlit talks.
So {partner} and you probably solve life problems under streetlights.
Quiet sky. Loud hearts. ...I like that.

questions.scene: Dillon writes 'sorry' on a napkin, then crosses it out, then writes it again.
lines: ...Apologies. I'm slow at them.
questions.question: Saying sorry: right away, or once you know exactly what to say?

choices.label: Right away
reply: ...Right away. Brave and fast.
Fixes things before they get heavy.

choices.label: Once I know what to say
reply: ...Once you know what to say. Thoughtful.
Better words, fewer regrets.

A:A: ...Both of you say sorry right away. Healthy.
Honestly, {partner} and you never let things sit too long.
...That's rare. Keep that.
A:B: ...You need time. {partner} apologizes right away.
They'll say sorry fast. You'll still be drafting.
Say 'I'm thinking.' Then take your time. ...That counts.
B:A: ...You say sorry right away. {partner} needs time to find words.
You'll apologize in seconds. They'll take an afternoon.
Their sorry is coming. It'll be a good one. ...Wait for it.
B:B: ...Both of you need time to find the words. Gentle couple.
I can picture it: you and {partner} would rather say it right than fast.
Just let each other know you're thinking. ...It helps.

questions.scene: Dillon flinches slightly when your doorbell rings.
lines: ...Surprises. They scare me. ...A little.
questions.question: Surprises: love them, or warn me first?

choices.label: Love them
reply: ...Love them. Fearless.
Confetti doesn't scare you. Wow.

choices.label: Warn me first
reply: ...Warn me first. Same.
A heads-up is kindness.

A:A: ...You both love surprises. Bold.
Pretty sure {partner} and you surprise each other constantly.
...Exciting. Exhausting. Mostly exciting.
A:B: ...You want a warning. {partner} loves surprises.
They'll plan secret things. You'll sense it and panic.
Ask for one hint. Just one. ...Then enjoy it.
B:A: ...You love surprises. {partner} wants a warning.
Give them a small heads-up. 'Something's coming. It's good.'
They'll relax. Then enjoy it more. ...Trust me.
B:B: ...You both want a warning. Safe couple.
Lowkey, you and {partner} say 'surprise on Friday!' before the surprise. Love it.
Predictable is cozy. ...Very cozy.

questions.scene: Dillon's paws fidget with a pebble the whole time he talks.
lines: ...I fidget when I'm nervous. You'll notice the pebble. Don't mention it.
questions.question: When your partner is nervous, what do their hands do?
questions.selfQuestion: When you're nervous, what do your hands do?

choices.label: Fidget with anything nearby
reply: ...Fidget. Pens, sleeves, pebbles.
Relatable. Very relatable.

choices.label: Reach for a hand to hold
reply: ...Reach for a hand. Brave.
Asking for comfort is strong.

A:A: ...Fidgeting, and {partner} knew it.
They've noticed you clicking the same pen twelve times.
Maybe hold their hand instead. ...Good fidget.
A:B: ...You reach for a hand. {partner} expected fidgeting.
They didn't realize their hand is your comfort.
Tell them. They'll keep it free for you. ...Always.
B:A: ...You fidget. {partner} thought you'd reach for their hand.
They're waiting with an open hand. You're holding a pebble.
Put the pebble down. Take the hand. ...Just try once.
B:B: ...Reaching for a hand, and {partner} knew it.
They know your hand finds theirs when things get tense.
That's trust. ...Real trust.

questions.scene: Dillon stares out the window at the road, deep in thought.
lines: ...Opening up is hard. Like a shell with a rusty hinge.
questions.question: What helps your partner open up the most?
questions.selfQuestion: What helps you open up the most?

choices.label: A late-night drive
reply: ...A drive. Side by side. Eyes on the road.
Easier to talk without staring.

choices.label: A long walk
reply: ...A walk. Moving helps the words.
Footsteps make room for feelings.

choices.label: Being under a blanket
reply: ...A blanket. Safe little cave.
Feelings come out when you're cozy.

A:A: ...A late-night drive, and {partner} knew it.
They've learned to take the long way home. On purpose.
...That's kind of beautiful.
A:B: ...A walk opens you up. {partner} guessed a drive.
They're starting the car. You're tying your shoes.
Drive to a park. Then walk. ...Both.
A:C: ...A blanket opens you up. {partner} guessed a drive.
They're grabbing car keys. You're grabbing the throw.
Tell them: no keys needed. Just blankets.
B:A: ...A drive opens you up. {partner} guessed a walk.
Close. You both like moving while talking.
Next time they say 'walk?', say 'drive?'
B:B: ...A long walk, and {partner} knew it.
They know your best talks happen around mile two.
Comfortable shoes. Open hearts.
B:C: ...A blanket opens you up. {partner} guessed a walk.
They're waiting by the door. You're on the couch.
Short walk, long blanket. ...Works for me.
C:A: ...A drive opens you up. {partner} guessed a blanket.
They're building a blanket fort. You're grabbing the keys.
Bring the blanket in the car. ...Compromise.
C:B: ...A walk opens you up. {partner} guessed a blanket.
They want you cozy. You want fresh air.
C:C: They know you talk best when you're wrapped up like a burrito.
...I'd do the same. Shell plus blanket.

questions.scene: Dillon shrugs one shoulder and says, very softly, '...Maybe.'
lines: ...What does that mean? Good question.
questions.question: When your partner says 'maybe,' what do they usually mean?
questions.selfQuestion: When you say 'maybe,' what do you usually mean?

choices.label: Yes, but nervous
reply: ...Yes, but nervous. That's my 'maybe.'
Means 'I want to. I'm scared.'

choices.label: No, but polite
reply: ...No, but polite. Diplomatic.
'Maybe' is the nicest 'no.'

A:A: ...'Maybe' means 'yes, nervously,' and {partner} knew it.
They hear the hidden 'yes' every time.
...That's real understanding. Keep it.
A:B: ...Your 'maybe' means no. {partner} thought it meant yes.
Oops. They've been buying tickets.
Try 'probably not.' ...Kinder in the long run.
B:A: ...Your 'maybe' means yes. {partner} thought it meant no.
They've been canceling plans you secretly wanted.
Next time, say 'maybe yes.' ...Tiny upgrade.
B:B: ...'Maybe' means 'no, politely,' and {partner} knew it.
They know not to buy the concert tickets.
...Saves everyone some money.

questions.scene: Dillon hands you the TV remote very slowly, like it's a sacred object.
lines: ...This is a big deal. I don't hand this to just anyone.
questions.question: How does your partner show they really trust you?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you show your partner you really trust them?

choices.label: Lets you see them cry
reply: ...Crying in front of someone. Huge.
That's real armor coming off.

choices.label: Hands over the TV remote
reply: ...The remote. Sacred trust.
Giving up control. ...Huge too.

A:A: ...Crying in front of them, and {partner} knew it.
They know your tears are the deepest trust you have.
...That means they're safe. Very safe.
A:B: ...You show trust with the remote. {partner} guessed tears.
They think it's deep. It's... also deep. In a TV way.
Both count. ...Remote trust is real trust.
B:A: ...You show trust through tears. {partner} guessed the remote.
They think it's the remote. It's much deeper.
Tell them. ...They'll treasure it.
B:B: ...The remote, and {partner} knew it.
They know handing over the remote is basically a marriage proposal.
...Ha. Respect.

questions.scene: A door slams down the hall. Dillon jumps a full foot, lands, and stares at you.
lines: ...Obviously relevant. Don't laugh.
questions.question: When your partner gets startled, what happens?
questions.selfQuestion: When you get startled, what happens?

choices.label: Jumps like an armadillo
reply: ...Jumps. Fellow jumper.
Vertical panic. I respect it.

choices.label: Freezes completely
reply: ...Freezes. Statue mode.
If I don't move, it can't see me.

A:A: ...Jumper, and {partner} knew it.
They've seen you leave the ground over a sneeze.
...Welcome to the club. I'm the president.
A:B: ...You freeze. {partner} thought you'd jump.
They're waiting for a leap. You just... stop.
...Statue mode. Also valid. Also scary.
B:A: ...You jump. {partner} thought you'd freeze.
They're about to see you hit the ceiling.
...Warn them. Or don't. It's funnier.
B:B: ...Freezer, and {partner} knew it.
They know you turn into a statue when a door slams.
...Very calm. Very still. Very scared.
